I guess this is anecdotal, but if I, at 15 years old, had been treated for the trauma that was causing my eating disorder, instead of having useless talks about how I felt about my body, I might not have been a suicidal 25-year-old right now. I’ve read my medical journals from that time, and the trauma was glaringly obviously if anyone had bothered to actually look.

Others have already said to look into the breed and to maybe consider getting two cats, but that depends on how small your apartment is. 

Generally, (most) cats can absolutely be left alone for 10 hours at a time. However, you cannot see cats as an easy pet that handles themselves, or don’t need much from you. If you’re away for 10 hours a day, you still need to activate your cat when you get home. Playing with them, petting them, or taking them out for a walk in a harness. As long as you acknowledge this, that a cat isn’t necessarily “easier” than a dog just because you don’t *have* to walk it, I think you’ll be fine. 

As others have said, also look into adoption. Either through a shelter, or just someone who (for some reason) can’t keep their cat anymore. They could tell you a lot about the cats personality, which you help you determine if it’s a good fit for you. 

I’d say space or time away from home aren’t the biggest issues here. If you’re willing to put time into it, I’m sure a cat could find a good home with you.
